sen_interval.note: scipy's theilslopes takes the same ranks as Gilbert (1987) 16.5, (N - C)/2 and (N + C)/2 + 1, but rounds them to whole ranks, computes its variance from the half-limit values and keeps the slope between two censored values as computed (the pipeline sets it to 0, as LWPTrends does); the pipeline interpolates between the two neighbouring slopes. The difference is therefore at most about half a rank step. Both rules are reproduced exactly from the slopes (see max_abs_difference).

headlines.text: Of the 203 wells sampled in 2021 to 2025, 107 (53%) had a five-year median above 5.65 mg/L, half the drinking-water limit, and 55 (27%) a median above the limit itself, 11.3 mg/L. 89 of the 203 have a single sample in those years, and the wells are not a representative network; counting only the 106 with at least three samples, 67 (63%) and 32 (30%).
headlines.how: wells in the area with at least one observation dated 2021-2025; each well's median of those observations (censored values at half the limit); counted where the median is > 5.65 and > 11.3 mg/L as N (strictly greater); single-sample wells: one observation in 2021-2025; the second count keeps wells with three or more

headlines.text: Over the ten years 2016 to 2025, 33 of the 54 wells with enough data (61%) were likely or very likely rising, 22 of them (41%) very likely; 14 (26%) were likely or very likely falling.
headlines.how: wells assessed for 2016-2025 under the data rules (method page); LAWA classes from the Mann-Kendall or seasonal Kendall test; 'likely or very likely rising' = confidence of an increase at least 67%; 'very likely' = at least 90%; the tie range from the sensitivity check that breaks equal distances to the later date

headlines.text: Over the twenty years 2006 to 2025, 41 of the 49 wells with enough data (84%) were likely or very likely rising (40 to 41 depending on how one tie between two sampling dates is broken), 36 of them (73%) very likely; 6 (12%) were likely or very likely falling.
headlines.how: wells assessed for 2006-2025 under the data rules (method page); LAWA classes from the Mann-Kendall or seasonal Kendall test; 'likely or very likely rising' = confidence of an increase at least 67%; 'very likely' = at least 90%; the tie range from the sensitivity check that breaks equal distances to the later date

headlines.text: Among the 49 wells assessed over 2006 to 2025, the typical (median) Sen slope was 0.13 mg/L a year, about 1.3 mg/L a decade; the middle half of wells lay between 0.05 and 0.23 mg/L a year.
headlines.how: the Sen slope (mg/L as N a year) of every well assessed for 2006-2025, whatever its class; median and quartiles (linear interpolation)

headlines.text: In the 19 wells sampled in every year from 2006 to 2025 (long-term monitoring wells, 11 of them between the Ashburton and the Rakaia and 1 of them 80 m or deeper), the median of the 19 wells went from 6.9 mg/L in 2006 to 9.6 mg/L in 2025; that median rose by 0.15 mg/L a year (Sen slope; very likely increasing).
headlines.how: wells with at least one observation in each year 2006-2025 (the same wells every year, so a changing network cannot make the trend); each well's yearly median, then the median across the wells; Mann-Kendall and Sen slope on those 20 yearly medians, time in whole years

headlines.text: Fewer deep wells (80 m or more) had a 2021–2025 median above the limit (4 of 33, 12%) than shallower wells (22 of 79 under 30 m; 29 of 91 at 30–80 m). Deep wells were not lower overall: their median was 6.75 mg/L against 4.6 mg/L under 30 m, and 20 of 33 were above half the limit.
headlines.how: as the first finding, split by the well's recorded depth (ECan's wells layer); the median is the median of the wells' five-year medians; Fisher's exact test on the counts above the limit is on the method page
